live_web_research.page_text: [2610.11572] PAM-ToD: Plug-and-Play Appearance Modeling for Cross-Time-of-Day 3D Gaussian Splatting Skip to main content Search arXiv Press Enter to search · Advanced search --> Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition arXiv:2610.11572 (cs) [Submitted on 8 Oct 2026] Title: PAM-ToD: Plug-and-Play Appearance Modeling for Cross-Time-of-Day 3D Gaussian Splatting Authors: Kota Shimomura , Sungho Moon , Tsubasa Hirakawa , Takayoshi Yamashita , Sunghoon Im , Hironobu Fujiyoshi View a PDF of the paper titled PAM-ToD: Plug-and-Play Appearance Modeling for Cross-Time-of-Day 3D Gaussian Splatting, by Kota Shimomura and 5 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Adapting a pre-trained 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) road scene to a new time of day requires learning appearance changes from a few anchor images while preserving consistent, real-time rendering. We propose PAM-ToD, a lightweight plug-in that learns color corrections while keeping the pre-trained 3DGS parameters fixed. PAM-ToD scales each Gaussian's existing color to model illumination changes and uses an additive term for additional brightness, such as when street lamps turn on at night. Under a simplified image formation model, unchanged surface albedo can be eliminated from the relation between source and target appearances, allowing us to learn these corrections without separately estimating albedo and illumination. The model corrects colors across the scene while allowing the corrections to vary by location and by Gaussian. To guide learning from a few anchor images, it discourages abrupt spatial changes in these corrections. We also introduce CARLA-ToD, a benchmark with matching geometry, camera poses, and moving-object trajectories across three times of day. A few target-time anchor images are used to train each plug-in, while separate views are used for evaluation. Across the static and dynamic settings, PAM-ToD achieves higher PSNR and lower LPIPS than the baselines, even when the anchor images come from a single synchronized capture across multiple cameras. selected_records.title: PAM-ToD: Plug-and-Play Appearance Modeling for Cross-Time-of-Day 3D Gaussian Splatting

article.body:
PAM-ToD adapts 3D Gaussian road scenes to different times of day

PAM-ToD is a plug-in method for changing the appearance of pre-trained 3D Gaussian Splatting road scenes. It targets users adapting those scenes to a new time of day: they can learn color corrections from a few target-time images without changing the scene’s pre-trained parameters.

The method scales each Gaussian’s existing color to model illumination and adds brightness where needed, such as from street lamps. The paper reports better PSNR and lower LPIPS than its baselines; these are author-reported results, not independent verification.

PAM-ToD is presented in an arXiv research paper, not as a released product. Software access and implementation availability are not specified.
